THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:40028  CRL.P No. 10918 of 2023  ORDER 1. Accused no.1 in Crime No.162/2023 registered by Mysuru City Women Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 324, 355, 504, 506, 149 of IPC, Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, and Section 4 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act,
2019, is before this Court under Section 438 Cr.PC.
2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Smt. Arjuman Banu @ Tanjiya Banu dated 16.09.2023,
FIR in Crime No.162/29023 was registered against the petitioner and others for the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text: Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl. Misc. No.1904/2023 before the Court of V Addl. Sessions Judge, Mysuru, which was dismissed as against him on 10.10.2023.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, submits that accused nos.4 & 5 have been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in NC: 2023:KHC:40028 Crl.P.No.10654/2023 and accused nos.2 & 3 have been granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court.
He, accordingly prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

6. From a perusal of the complaint averments, it is seen that the complainant who is the wife of the petitioner herein has filed a detailed typed complaint on 16.09.2023 making allegations that the petitioner and other accused persons were harassing and torturing her in her matrimonial home and they were abusing and assaulting her.
7. Omnibus allegations are made in the complaint against all the accused.
From a reading of the complaint, it is seen that the petitioner allegedly had pronounced Talak against the complainant and had thrown her out from his house on 31.08.2023.
The complaint is belatedly lodged on 16.09.2023.
The offences alleged against the accused are triable by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment by three years.
Accused nos.2 & 3 have been granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court and accused nos.4 & 5 have been granted Ajmal Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka on 8 November, 2023

Under the circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the following order:
8.
The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.162/2023 registered by Mysuru City Women Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 324, 355, 504, 506, 149 of IPC, Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, and Section 4 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with NC:
2023:KHC:40028 the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
